**STEP 1 - Scene:** A side dish of cooked (boiled or steamed) sliced carrots on a plate, with no visible sauce or garnish.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** A white square, slightly curved plate, about 21 cm per side, so roughly a side plate. Because it is square, I used side × side rather than the circle formula: area ≈ 21 × 21 ≈ 440 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Cooked carrot slices, about 18 coins and diagonal ovals. There is a slight moist sheen but no visible oil or butter.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The carrots cover about 22% of the plate. That is the total food coverage.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** 22% × 440 cm² ≈ 97 cm². The slices overlap and pile up in places, so I used a pile height of about 1.5 cm. 97 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 145 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Cut vegetables have a bulk density of about 0.65 g/ml. 145 ml × 0.65 ≈ 94 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Boiled carrots have about 35 kcal per 100 g. 94 g × 0.35 ≈ 33 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 18 cooked carrot slices, roughly one large carrot, would weigh around 90–100 g. The estimate is plausible.
